title: What is known about 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE---: it halts (Lean).
intro: This six-state machine is on the bbchallenge list of holdouts. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. The headline: it halts from blank tape, proved in Lean.
verdict: It halts, proved in Lean (theorem halts_from_blank). The machine is a small rewriting system on the right half of its tape (the visit law, kernel-checked): blocks 000/100 are binary digits, blocks 1010 double the visits passing through, and a visit that meets 1011 halts. A checker for this system, proved correct in the kernel, finds that rounds 1 to 161,210 only rewrite and that round 161,211 meets 1011; that evaluation is by native_decide (compiled code), in ten segments. It halts after between 6.3 × 1024,266 and 1.08 × 1024,267 steps (computed, not proved).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: Both counters' increments, for all sizes
claims.text: At an event (A on cell 3; left of it the block 011001 and the left counter in digits 0110 = 0 / 0111 = 1; right of it the phase cell, the block 001010000 and the right counter, digits three cells apart): the left increment with a carry over n ones (22n+34 steps), the right increment on a lowest 0 (42) and over k+1 ones (6k+48), carries across one junk unit 1010000 (84, 90) and across j units then k+1 ones (36j+6k+54). 6 theorems.

claims.title: The visit law, in two forms
claims.text: A visit (the head on a 0 with a 0 on its left and a stream s on its right, in state C or F; it returns in state A two cells further left) rewrites the stream by 0 s → 1 s, 100 s → 000 v(s), 110 s → 000 v(s), 1010 s → 1010 v(v(s)), and halts the machine on 1011 s; for every stream and every left tape. Form W obeys the rules for 0, 100, 1010, 1011; it has no such rule for 110 (W_1100: 1100 s → 1010 v(s)). The run is a sequence of rounds 0^inf A> 1 0 0 S → 0^inf A> 1 0 0 v(1 0 S), starting after 6 steps with S = 1 0^inf.

claims.title: The abstract visit law and its count laws
claims.text: The four rules and the halting pattern as inductive relations on streams, with no machine in them; the 1010 rule is guarded (the stream behind must not start with 11), and after two visits a stream never starts with 11. Under n visits, 000 r and 100 r are binary digits that pass every second visit on, and 1010 r passes 2n visits on; likewise for "one of the first n visits halts".

claims.title: A checker for the visit law, proved correct
claims.text: scan carries a count of visits, kept as the pair e, c for 2e − c, through a finite word in one pass; hscan looks for a halting visit. Both are proved against the abstract system.

claims.title: If the checker accepts, the machine halts
claims.text: This machine satisfies the law, so for every k: if the checker runs k rounds from the word 1 and then finds a halting visit in the next round, the machine halts from blank tape. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

claims.title: The machine halts from blank tape
claims.text: check 161210 [true] = true: rounds 1 to 161,210 use the four rewriting rules only, round 161,211 meets 1011. Evaluated with the checker compiled to native code, in ten segments chained by a kernel-checked lemma (about 3 hours of computing in all; the word grows to 1,001,253 cells). With the claim above: the machine halts. Besides the three standard axioms the theorem depends on eleven native_decide axioms, one per evaluation (trust in the Lean compiler). The number of steps is bounded separately (computed). Each segment was checked on 13 and 14 November 2026, and the whole check was run again from start to end on 14 November 2026 (HALT CHECKED). The repository's automatic checks cover the kernel-only part, not this evaluation.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 248 cells have been visited and 98 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 1011 steps (longrun.c, the simulator of tools/c/tm.h) without a halt.

claims.title: The left side is clockwork
claims.text: Between consecutive left-end extensions the busiest cell turns 3·2<sup>k</sup> times, each count twice (48, 96, 96, ..., 3·2<sup>22</sup>), in the first 1.5·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: How much of the run the increments cover
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps (879,588 events) 95.5% of the events are instances of these theorems (left 439,766; right0 219,887; right1 92,325; junk_10 57,511; junk_110 28,751; junk_jk 1,733); the other 39,615 are carries over other junk layouts and the moments around the ends.

claims.title: The same round as the PR59 machines
claims.text: The three machines of busycoq PR59 (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- and two relatives) obey the same law with one form of visit, and PR59 proves in Rocq that they halt in round 161,211. The proof here does not use PR59; our C simulator of the law (vis.c) also halts in that round on the PR59 machine. The twin 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- has its own theorem: machines with related tables are not claimed to halt together.

claims.title: Between 6.3 × 10<sup>24,266</sup> and 1.08 × 10<sup>24,267</sup> steps
claims.text: Computed, not proved: the machine halts after between 6.3 × 1024,266 and 1.08 × 1024,267 steps (190.3·280605 to 323.1·280605). Every visit costs a fixed number of steps of its own: 4 or 8 steps for 0 → 1, 6 or 8 for 100, 10 for 110, 22 or 24 for 1010 (entered in C or F). A C program repeats the checker's pass for all 161,210 rounds and adds up the visits per rule (5.9519·280605 of each main kind in the completed rounds, at most 2.1164·280605 more in the halting round). Its final word agrees cell for cell with the word the Lean segments check; the sums are in floating point, and the bounds are widened by 0.1% for that.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Two counters of the same events
claims.text: Read off the run: the counters on the two sides of the engine both go up by 1 at every visit of the head to the engine, one of them with fixed junk stretches between some digits; the junk is written when a carry reaches the end of the tape.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

check: holdouts/1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE---/lean/check_halt.sh   # the halting theorem: compiles the checker, then ten native_decide segments, about 3 hours

explainer.lede: Yes, it halts, and Lean has checked the proof. Behind two counters ticking together this machine is a small rewriting system: blocks 000/100 that act as binary digits, blocks 1010 that double the visits passing through, and a block 1011 that stops the machine. For 161,210 rounds the trap never forms; in round 161,211 it does. Nobody could watch that happen: it takes about 1024,266 steps.

facts.text: halts_from_blank, proved in Lean (kernel + native_decide for the checker run).
The machine as a rewriting system on streams; the checker and its correctness proof.
The first round in which a visit meets 1011.

sections.heading: From six states to one computation
html: "Does this machine halt?" is answered here by walking down five levels of description. Each level forgets
detail the one above it keeps, and each step down is a Lean theorem that carries the answer back up: a halt found
at a lower level is a halt of the level above. At the bottom there is no machine left, only one computation, and
running that computation is the last link of the proof (the bottom line).
A tape of cells and a head in one of six states. One unit of time is one step.
From blank tape to the halt: between 6.3·1024,266 and 1.08·1024,267 steps (computed, not proved).
Level 2Rounds and visits
At the start of every round the tape is 0∞ A> 1 0 0 S; a round is one
visit to the word 1 0 S, which makes visits of its own, entered in state C or F. One unit is one round.
Kernel a halting round is a halt of the machine: start, round, round_halts, V_*, W_*
Level 3Four rules on words
The visit as a rewriting system on words of 0s and 1s, with a trap 1011, and no machine in it.
Kernel every abstract visit is a visit of the machine: law, Law.av, Law.ah
One pass per round carries the number of visits, written 2e − c, through the word.
One unit is one block of the word.
Kernel the pass gives what the visits give: scan_sound, hscan_sound, halts_of_check

sections.heading: Rounds and visits
html: Call everything from some cell to the right a stream. A visit: the head stands on a 0 (the lead
cell) with a 0 on its left and a stream s on its right, in state C (form V) or in state F (form W); it comes back
in state A two cells further left, both 0s restored and s rewritten. lean/Visit.lean proves, for every
stream and every tape to the left, what a visit does to a stream according to how the stream begins. The theorems
were produced by running the transition table symbolically on every short beginning of a stream
(py/visit2.py), and each proof is an exact count of the machine's own steps between the nested

"Then V" means: the machine makes a visit of its own, in form V, to the stream behind the block, whose lead

cell is the last cell of the block. In this machine the two forms are not the same. Entered in F, a visit obeys the rules for 0, 100, 1010 and 1011, but on 1100 s it writes 1010 and visits s once (W_1100), and on 1101 and 111 it has no rule of this shape at all. A visit in form W is only ever made as the first of the two nested visits behind a doubler 1010. If a nested visit halts, so does the visit around it
Rounds. From blank tape the machine reaches 0∞ A> 1 0 0 1 0∞
after 6 steps (start). From a tape 0∞ A> 1 0 0 S it takes 8 steps to
stand on the first of these cells in state C, with 1 0 S as its stream, and a visit then brings it to
0∞ A> 1 0 0 S', two cells further left, where S' is what the visit made of
1 0 S (round); if that visit halts, the machine halts (round_halts). So the
whole run is a sequence of rounds, and each round is one visit with visits nested inside it.

sections.heading: The same rules without the machine
html: Leave out the states, the step counts and the two forms, and what remains is a rewriting system on words. In
VisitLaw.lean it is two inductive relations on streams with no machine in them: AV s s',
"one visit rewrites s to s'", and AH s, "a visit to s halts".
100 r000, and one visit to rAV.h
110 r000, and one visit to rAV.g
1010 r1010, and two visits to r, if r does not start with 11AV.l
A visit also halts if one of its nested visits halts (AH.h, AH.g, AH.l1,
AH.l2). So a block 000 or 100 is a binary digit: it flips on every
visit and passes every second visit on. A block 1010 is a doubler: it passes every visit on
The guard. The doubler rule carries the side condition "the stream behind does not start with

11" (Guard), because the first of its two nested visits is made in form W. In this machine form W has no rule for 110, so the doubler rule can only be turned into visits of the machine when the stream behind the doubler does not start with 11. Lean
proves that after two visits a stream never starts with 11 (av2_guard), and the checker
below tests the condition every time it uses the rule.
From the rules to the machine. Law lists what a machine's two forms must satisfy, one field
per rule, and Law.av, Law.ah turn every abstract visit into a visit of the machine in
form V (and in form W when the guard holds). lean/Law.lean fills in the fields with the theorems of
the table above (law); everything is checked by the kernel.

sections.heading: Counting visits instead of making them
html: After k rounds the word begins with about k/2 doublers, so about 2k/2 visits reach the blocks behind
them, and round 161,211 could never be replayed visit by visit. But all the visits that reach one block are
alike, so it is enough to know how many there are. VisitLaw.lean proves what n visits in a row
do (VS n s s', for every n):
• 000 r under n visits ends as the digit n mod 2, and ⌊n/2⌋ visits reach r (law_Z);
• 100 r ends as the digit (n + 1) mod 2, and ⌈n/2⌉ visits reach r (law_H); the same for
• 1010 r stays 1010, and 2n visits reach r (vs_L, with the guard on r);
• a 0 where a block should start takes the first visit to become a 1 (law_0);
• and the same laws for "one of the first n visits halts" (hvs_Z, hvs_H, hvs_G,
Try a law: the browser makes n visits one by one with the rewriting rules and counts how many of them reach the
stream r behind the block (here r starts as blank tape).

The pass. The checker (scan in VisitCheck.lean) carries the number of visits through
the word block by block, in one pass, using these laws: through a doubler n visits become 2n; through a digit n
becomes n/2, rounded down or up depending on the digit, and the digit is set to the parity of n; when the count
reaches 0 the rest of the word is copied unchanged. The counts are huge but simple: each is a power of two minus a
small number, so the checker keeps a count as a pair e, c standing for 2<sup>e</sup> − c, and doubling is
e + 1, halving is e − 1. scan_sound proves that what the pass returns is what 2e − c
visits of the rewriting system make; hscan_sound proves the same for its search for a halting visit
(sound, not complete: when it is unsure it answers no).

sections.heading: 161,210 rounds, then the trap
html: What is left is a program. round s is one pass of scan over the word 1 0 s
with a single visit (e = c = 0); iter k s makes k rounds and fails if a round fails, as it does when a
positive count meets 1011; and check k s makes k rounds and then asks hscan whether
the next round has a halting visit. halts_of_check_blank (lean/Law.lean, kernel, with the
three standard axioms) says: if check k [true] = true for some k, the machine halts from blank tape. The
word [true] is the word 1 after the 6 steps of start.
So the proof needs the value of one expression, check 161210 [true]. That is about 1011 list
operations, too many for the kernel, so Lean compiles the checker to native code and evaluates it
(native_decide). The run is cut into ten segments, each "k rounds take the word after a rounds to the
word after b rounds", with the words at the boundaries (up to a million cells) written into the proof as numbers
(VisitW*.lean); a kernel-checked lemma, iter_add, chains the segments, and an eleventh

The checker, the rewriting system and the segment files live in the folder of the twin machine, holdouts/1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE---/lean/, because they do not depend on the machine: the same evaluation serves both machines, and each machine has its own Visit.lean, Law.lean and Halt.lean. The segments took 10 to 30 minutes each, about 3 hours of computing in all. Each
segment was checked once (13 and 14 November 2026); the whole check was then run again from start to end on a fresh

clone on 14 November 2026 for the twin (the commands of check_halt.sh, with the ten segments four at a time, about 40 minutes on four cores), and this machine's Halt.lean was compiled against those segments; both printed HALT CHECKED. The repository's automatic checks run check.sh (the kernel-only

sections.heading: It halts
html: Started on a blank tape, the machine 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- stops: in round 161,211 a visit meets the block
1011, and the head, in state F, reads a 1. That happens after between 6.3 × 1024,266 and 1.08 × 1024,267 steps (computed, not
HaltsFromBlank is the machine's own halting from blank tape, defined from its transition table in

The machine obeys the rulesFor every stream and every left tape, a visit in either form does what the table of rules says, a round is one visit, and the run starts with the word 1 (lean/Visit.lean, generated from the transition table).Kernel
The rules, without the machineThe rewriting system and its count laws (VisitLaw.lean), and the fact that this machine satisfies it (law, lean/Law.lean).Kernel

The program computes the rulesscan and hscan return what the rewriting system gives, so if check k [true] = true the machine halts (VisitCheck.lean, halts_of_check_blank). Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.Kernel
The run itselfcheck 161210 [true] = true: ten segments and the halting round, chained by iter_add (VisitRun.lean, VisitSeg*.lean).native_decide eleven evaluations; the chaining by the kernel
So everything is checked by Lean's kernel except the evaluation of a checker that is itself proved correct.
That evaluation is by native_decide, compiled code, and the theorem depends on eleven
native_decide axioms, one per evaluation (trust in the Lean compiler; the comment in
Halt.lean names it Lean.ofReduceBool), besides the three standard axioms. The halting
theorem is checked by lean/check_halt.sh, about 3 hours of computing; the repository's automatic checks
run check.sh, the kernel-only part, but not this evaluation.
Elsewhere. The same visit law, in a Coq proof on busycoq's definitions (tools/coq/busycoq/VisitLaw2/,
halts : halts tm c0, Coq 8.20.1, no axioms): the checker of busycoq PR59 extended to two forms of
visit, with the whole run as one vm_compute of about 15 minutes. And the three machines of busycoq PR59
(1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- and two relatives) obey the same law with one form of visit,
entered one cell further left; PR59 proves in Rocq that they halt in round 161,211. The Lean proof here does not use
PR59, so that both land on the same round is a cross-check (as is the C simulator
holdouts/1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---/c/vis.c, which halts in that round on the PR59
machine). The twin 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- halts in the same round by the same checker run; that is a separate theorem
about a different table, not a consequence of this one.
Between 6.3 × 1024,266 and 1.08 × 1024,267 steps from blank tape to the halt, that is 190.3·280605 to 323.1·280605. A number with 24,267 digits (or
24,268): large, but an ordinary power, not a power tower.
Every visit costs a fixed number of the machine's own steps, apart from its nested visits: 4 or 8 steps for 0 → 1, 6 or 8 for 100, 10 for 110, 22 or 24 for 1010, entered in C or F (the step
numbers in the proofs of lean/Visit.lean, the ones the panel on rounds and visits checks against the
machine). So the step count is the number of visits of each kind times these costs. c/steps.c in
holdouts/1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE---/ repeats the checker's pass for all 161,210 rounds and
adds up the counts per rule: in the completed rounds there are 5.9519·2<sup>80605</sup> visits each of the
kinds 0 → 1, 100 and 1010 (the largest single count is 280605, in
round 161,210: the count in round r peaks at 2<sup>r/2</sup>), and at most 2.1164·2<sup>80605</sup> more of each
in the halting round, which stops part of the way through. The lower bound takes the completed rounds at the
cheaper cost, the upper bound adds the whole halting round at the dearer cost.
The program's word after 161,210 rounds agrees cell for cell with the word in VisitW161210.lean, which
the Lean segments check; the sums are kept as a mantissa and an exponent in floating point (the bounds are widened
by 0.1% for that). Lean's theorems say "after some number of steps" and do not state the numbers. Nothing in these
Nothing for the halting question. Open ends: a Lean proof of the step bounds (they are computed), and a proof of
the evaluation inside the kernel (it is about 1011 list operations, too many for kernel reduction).

sections.heading: Two counters and an engine
html: Before the visit law was found, the run was described as two counters ticking together. That description is kept here: it is how the run looks at the level of the machine, and parts of it are Lean theorems of their own (lean/Rules.lean, lean/Events.lean).

Most of the time the tape is L · engine · R. Each visit of the head to the engine is an event, and every event adds 1 to both counters. In the reference machine of the family (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---), L is written in blocks of four cells, 0101 for a 1 and 0001 for a 0, lowest digit next to the engine, and R keeps one cell per digit, three cells apart (the cells 9, 12, 15, … right of the head), lowest digit nearest the engine. 1,572,0210001 0001 0101 000100101 00000 000 000 001 00098

(The block of L touching the engine is always 0001; the low bits shown are the next three blocks. The carries are sweeps proved in Lean for every length; in the reference machine r_up and r_down carry the right counter over k ones in 5k + 13 and 3k + 18 steps.)

This machine is a relative in different clothes: its left counter has 4-cell digits x011, its left-end extensions come after exactly 3·2k turns of the busiest cell, each count twice, and at its left-end visits the tape is that of the reference family: at step 14,008,454 its 183-cell tape agrees with that of 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- at step 9,617,068 in all cells but the first two.

When L overflows, the carry runs to the left end of the tape, the tape grows by two cells there, and L starts again. The lowest digit of L is the cell where the head turns most often, and the number of its turns between two consecutive left-end extensions follows a strict pattern, without a single exception in the first 1.5·109 steps (ymax.c):

48 96 96 192 192 384 384 … 3·221 3·221 3·222

So the periods of the left side are powers of two in events, each length twice (the counter gains one digit every two periods). The time per event is not constant, because a carry on the right costs more when it crosses junk, so the steps between left-end extensions grow by factors between about 1.35 and 2.05 instead of exactly 2.
A counter with junk between its digits

The cells that change between events are the digits of the counters: each digit changes about half as often as the one before (chg.c counts, over a whole period, how often each cell changes from one event to the next). On the right, between some digits of R, there are stretches of fixed cells (0101010101 00 1 00 1 00 1 and the like) that the carries cross without changing. They are written when a carry runs into the end of the tape, at irregular event counts, and their layout is what makes the run irregular. How they are produced is not decoded yet.

The machine halts only in state F reading a 1, and F is entered from C1 (0RF) only. After C1, used about 2.9·107 times in 109 steps, the head has read a 0 every time (F0 is used exactly as often). Unlike the other members this machine has no rare transition: every transition is used more than 107 times in 109 steps. Halting would need that ordinary step to find a 1. In every run short enough to simulate directly this has not happened. The proof on this page shows that it does happen, in round 161,211.

This machine runs the reference's two counters with other words: the left digits are 0110 (0) and 0111 (1), the engine blocks are 011001 and 001010000, and the right counter with its junk units is the reference's. lean/Events.lean proves each kind of visit to the engine for every size. In the first 108 steps 95.5% of the 879,588 visits are instances of these theorems.

The family (G11-Y): 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (the reference), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (the same run), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- (all with left-end extensions after 2k events, each twice, to within a few hundred steps of each other); 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- and 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- (the same right part, a differently written left counter); and the mirror case 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---, with the junk on the left.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 248 cells (86 left of the start, 149 right), with a density of 1s of 0.395.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE---: 9,132,095 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,132,094 there

summary: Halts (Lean, with native_decide for the evaluation of a verified checker): a rewriting system on streams (visit law, kernel-checked) whose round 161,211 meets the halting block 1011; the same law and round as the busycoq PR59 machines, proved here independently.
family: PR59 visit law, entered one cell further right in two forms (halts on 1011 in round 161,211)
